title: Release through devbin's reshaped core: Utilz's side of Devbin ST0011/10
objective: Utilz releases through devbin's reshaped release core (Devbin ST0011) and keeps nothing of its own that does the core's work: no CI poller, formula writer, tag reader, macOS stager or hand dispatch beside it. Devbin's ST0011/10 points here.
context:
devbin-vc holds hv's pen for Devbin's ST0011 (hv's word in utilz-vc's session, 31 Oct 2026; vc's decision 75). This thread takes effect after ST0011/10's vendor sweep, which waits for hv's go on devbin's release (ST0011/09). devbin-vc's list of what changes for Utilz, with its rulings of 31 Oct:

- tools/ci-state, tools/post-cut and tools/formula retire into the core. install.sh's install_ci_state is a second CI reader, and it retires onto `bin/devbin ci-state`.
- In bin/.devbin/config.yaml, gates: gains `test estate` as a recorded gate run in parallel, macos: stays, and after: becomes `formula publish`. The built-in formula publish takes over the ST0030 tap pull, which Devbin's cc has.
- .github/workflows/tests.yml fires its macOS legs on candidate/ and loses its tag trigger. The hand dispatch and the dry run's `check all` stop. tools/test-estate and CI's menuz-app test build stay.
- docs/releasing.md follows.
- A risk: menuz gives MenuzKind=release only to a build of the tag (opt/menuz/menuz:632), but the core stages at the release commit, before the tag exists. menuz must read the stamp, not the tag.

dc's inventory at 48c0ea54, checked by vc and sent to devbin-vc as (1) on 31 Oct, says what names each path and what duplicates the core. The five ci-state tests at opt/utilz/test/install_lib.bats:767-828 are ST0019's AT01 on AC-01.3, so removing them goes through `intent at` on ST0019. opt/utilz/test/formula.bats tests tools/formula whole. vc's (2), sent the same day, is the baseline for ST0011/15. Issue 0131 (CI's headless Chrome stalls) gets its fix separately from this thread.
